title: PowerPoint on the web: reference an attached deck's style when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the briefing leaves the licence tier unresolved even though Microsoft's service description identifies Edit with Copilot as requiring a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, and Microsoft says this experience was previously called Agent Mode. The roadmap facts and the licence-assignment path and command are supported.

claims.quote: When creating a presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint using Agent Mode, you can reference an existing PowerPoint file
claims.fix: Keep Agent Mode as the roadmap's terminology, but qualify its first use: 'Microsoft now calls the experience Edit with Copilot; the roadmap calls it Agent Mode.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/copilot-frontier/get-started-editing-with-copilot-in-office, which says the former name is no longer used.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published which licence tier covers this Agent Mode capability.

Microsoft's support guidance says this experience was previously called Agent Mode.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/microsoft-365-copilot and https://support.microsoft.com/office/copilot-frontier/get-started-editing-with-copilot-in-office. claims.claim: No rate specific to attached-deck style referencing is published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference attached deck style pricing meter Copilot Credits limits. Read the item entry, Copilot overview, licence options and service description; found product entitlement but no separate attached-deck meter or rate.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a user licence using Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()
